conflicts.explanation: Retinoids and AHAs both stress the skin. Using them on the same night raises the risk of redness and peeling.
conflicts.source_title: British Skin Foundation: Which pharmaceutical skincare you shouldn't mix and why

conflicts.explanation: Retinoids and salicylic acid can dry and irritate skin when layered. Dermatologists suggest alternate nights, or using the acid as a face wash.
conflicts.source_title: Yahoo/Byrdie: AHAs/BHAs vs Retinol, dermatologists explain

conflicts.explanation: Benzoyl peroxide is an oxidiser and can break down retinoids, and the pair is irritating. Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and the retinoid at night.
conflicts.source_title: Martin et al. 1998, British Journal of Dermatology (PubMed)

conflicts.explanation: Benzoyl peroxide can degrade vitamin C, so the vitamin C stops working. Keep them in different routines.
conflicts.source_title: British Skin Foundation: Which pharmaceutical skincare you shouldn't mix and why

conflicts.explanation: Vitamin C and retinoids together can cause redness. Vitamin C in the morning, retinoid at night.
conflicts.source_title: British Skin Foundation: Which pharmaceutical skincare you shouldn't mix and why

conflicts.explanation: Vitamin C with AHAs can leave skin irritated, dry and flaky. Vitamin C in the morning, AHA at night.
conflicts.source_title: British Skin Foundation: Which pharmaceutical skincare you shouldn't mix and why

conflicts.explanation: Common myth. A cosmetic chemist's review found no loss of benefit and no skin damage from using niacinamide and vitamin C together.
conflicts.source_title: KindofStephen (cosmetic chemist): Niacinamide and Vitamin C

timing.explanation: Night only. Beginners start on alternate nights and build up slowly.
timing.source_title: American Academy of Dermatology: Retinoid or retinol?

timing.explanation: Night only, because AHAs make skin more sensitive to the sun. Wear sunscreen every morning. Leave-on exfoliating acids are limited to a few nights a week.
Leave-on exfoliating acids are limited to a few times a week. Over-exfoliating leaves skin red and irritated.
timing.source_title: American Academy of Dermatology news release: Evaluate before you exfoliate

timing.explanation: Morning use is generally recommended for vitamin C.
timing.source_title: British Skin Foundation: Which pharmaceutical skincare you shouldn't mix and why
